chapters.reason: The paper introduces TESS 2, a diffusion language model trained by adapting an autoregressive model with cross-entropy as diffusion loss, which aligns with embedding-based diffusion models that operate on continuous token embeddings and use denoising processes, as opposed to masked or hybrid approaches.

TESS 2 is adapted from a strong autoregressive model and integrates autoregressive components through continued pretraining and instruction tuning, fitting the hybrid AR-diffusion paradigm that combines both autoregressive and diffusion methods for improved performance.

The paper proposes reward guidance, an inference-time guidance procedure that aligns model outputs without retraining, which resembles test-time training methods that perform optimization steps during inference to enhance performance, though it is not explicitly based on SGD or Adam.
